record.notes: Published on 26 July 2024, developed per Section 4.1(a)(i)(A) of Executive Order 14110 (US-04) as a companion resource to the AI RMF (US-02), and informed by NIST's Generative AI Public Working Group, which focused on governance, content provenance, pre-deployment testing and incident disclosure. NIST's publication page lists it as published and was last updated on 8 April 2026.

verification.note: Recheck of 17 Oct 2026: the NIST publication page was stored again on 17 Oct 2026 (only its topic keywords and 'Accessed' date changed) and confirms the title, NIST AI 600-1, its DOI, 26 Jul 2024, the link to EO 14110 and the page's last update on 8 Apr 2026. The profile itself (NIST AI 600-1 PDF on nvlpubs.nist.gov) was stored in this run and confirms the twelve risks, the suggested actions and Section 4.1(a)(i)(A) of EO 14110. Version 1's count of more than 200 suggested actions is not stated in the text and was dropped, as was its speculative remark that the profile may be affected by the AI RMF revision.

record.summary: Cross-sectoral profile of, and companion resource to, the AI Risk Management Framework for generative AI. It defines twelve risks unique to or exacerbated by generative AI: CBRN information or capabilities; confabulation; dangerous, violent or hateful content; data privacy; environmental impacts; harmful bias or homogenization; human-AI configuration; information integrity; information security; intellectual property; obscene, degrading or abusive content; and value chain and component integration. It sets out suggested actions, organized by AI RMF subcategories, to govern, map, measure and manage these risks.
